root_idea.summary: The root centers on directedness and support: standing or extending upright, directing oneself toward an object, and relying on something that sustains or bears weight.
root_idea.development: From upright supports and things relied upon, the lexicon develops meanings of intention, purpose, reliance, structural support, central members, and states produced by pressure or bearing.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form V perfect citation form.
Displayed as the plural or quasi-plural noun عَمَدٌ.
Displayed as the distinct noun عِمَادٌ.
Displayed under the normalized active-participle citation form.

senses.definition: To do deliberately or intentionally; to intend an act on purpose.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction تَعَمَّدَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ, it describes deliberate intention rather than inadvertence.
In the descriptions of the heavens, the supports may be understood as visible pillars or as pillars not seen; the same noun also denotes ordinary supporting posts.

senses.definition: Extended pillars or columns of fire.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quranic construction describing the punishment in which the pillars are extended; this is a contextualized Quranic use of the pillar term, not a conversion of Lane’s historical citation notation into a modern location.

senses.definition: Supporting pillars or lofty structures; in إِرَمَ ذَاتِ الْعِمَادِ, the expression refers to Iram associated with lofty buildings supported by columns, or, in an alternative interpretation, with height and tallness.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic phrase has several classical interpretations, including lofty buildings, tallness, or both; the verse location is independently secured by QAC.

senses.definition: Deliberate, intentional; acting knowingly and on purpose.
senses.usage_conditions: An active participle describing an intentional act, including intentional killing or intentional violation in the Quranic examples; no object-class restriction is implied.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stay, prop up, support, or place columns or props beneath something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a wall or another supported object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike or beat, especially with an iron weapon; also to strike the abdomen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct Form I verbal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To intend, purpose, direct oneself toward, seek, aim at, or resort to someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The constructions عَمَدَ لَهُ, عَمَدَ إِلَيْهِ, and related transitive uses express directed purpose or recourse; doing something عَمْدًا adds earnest, certain intention.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To press heavily upon, oppress, pain, cause to fall, or grieve.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of disease, confinement, straitness, captivity, or another afflicting condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of earth, to become moistened by rain and compacted, especially layer upon layer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The moisture has sunk into the soil sufficiently for it to clump when grasped.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become swollen or internally damaged through pressure, injury, or premature squeezing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a camel’s hump or buttocks and to a pustule; the same group of evidence also includes suffering pain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become angry with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate reported verbal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a disputed idiomatic expression, to wonder at something; alternatives reported include being angry at it or lamenting it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression and its interpretation are explicitly reported as uncertain and disputed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To keep to, cling to, or adhere to a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction with بِهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stop or obstruct the course of a torrent so that its water collects in a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The obstruction may be made with earth, stones, or similar material.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To baptize someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Christian technical use, reported as an Arabic or Syriac-derived term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render someone dependent on support or unable to sit without being propped up.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported in a dialectal or traditional expression concerning the legs and a sick person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become stayed, propped up, or supported.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a wall or another thing that has become supported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lean, recline, bear, or rest upon something; figuratively, to rely upon a person or a book.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The figurative sense develops from physical reliance or support.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be syntactically dependent upon what precedes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A grammatical technical use, such as an epithet depending on its noun or an objective complement on its verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of rain, to rest upon and soak into the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported construction describing rainfall settling into earth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To travel at a gentle pace, including to ride on during the night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A travel-related use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To direct oneself to someone with something, or bring that thing to him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction with بِهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A swelling with galls in the back of a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use distinct from the verbal and plural-support uses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rain-moistened earth compacted into clumps or layers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to soil whose moisture has penetrated deeply.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a reported expression, abundant in goodness, beneficence, or bounty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transmitted text is partially corrupted, but the lexical explanation is recoverable in outline.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a hump internally broken or swollen from riding or saddle injury; also swollen from premature squeezing, as of a pustule.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied principally to a camel or pustule; the poetic cloud comparison is illustrative rather than a separate sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stay, prop, support, or object of reliance; a person or thing upon which another rests or depends.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May denote the support of an affair, a relied-upon person, or the mainstay of a people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An indispensable member of a proposition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A grammatical technical use, contrasted with a supplementary element.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An intention, purpose, aim, or chosen course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions meaning to keep to one’s intention or course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place that swells or becomes inflated in the hump and withers of a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical camel term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A youthful person full of vigor; also a bulky, corpulent, and tall person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form can describe a bulky woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tall, especially when applied to a man or woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A related descriptive form with feminine usage also attested.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man whose dwelling is a place known for its visitors.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression based on the tent-pole image.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person of exalted nobility or high standing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression meaning literally one with a high pole of the tent of nobility.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tent-pole, or a column or pillar of a house or similar structure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The primary concrete noun; also used for a tent supported by poles.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lord, master, chief, or commander upon whom a people or army relies.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from the support provided by a pillar.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A staff or stick.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete extension of the pole meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An iron weapon, rod, or mace used for striking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Distinct from the general staff or pole sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bar of iron or another metal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A material-object use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A perpendicular or upright line or object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geometric or positional extension of uprightness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slender, lofty mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in a poetic expression concerning an eagle’s nest.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Either upright support of a well’s pulley structure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two uprights together are called the two supports.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Either leg of a male ostrich.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional anatomical zoological term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A star identified with the upright timber of the cross in the constellation Delphinus.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A traditional astronomical name.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The beam of a balance or steelyard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical term for the horizontal balancing member.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The longitudinal ridge or raised line in the broad side of a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A sword-making and weapon term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The central ridge running along a spearhead between its cutting sides.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical weapon term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The back, or a central vein-like structure extending through the abdomen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is variously applied to the back, the central abdominal structure, or a vein from the lower sternum toward the navel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To carry something on one’s back; figuratively, to bear it with difficulty and fatigue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic use associated with the supporting function of the back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A central ligament, vein, or pair of large veins associated with the liver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The anatomical referent varies among authorities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The watīn, identified here with the aorta.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical designation based on the idea of support.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The main supporting part of the ear, or its rounded upper portion above the lobe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical term with variant explanations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The middle of the heart lengthwise, or a vein associated with it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also occurs in an expression meaning to place something in the center of one’s heart.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The middle of the tongue lengthwise.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The text or main body of a book.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use of the central supporting member.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The bright, spreading gleam of true dawn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression denotes the dawn that fills the horizon and begins the day.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The dust raised or extended by a whirlwind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A weather expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tallness of stature.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The state of distance from one’s friends in which travelers continue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The curl or feather of hair on a horse’s neck near the collar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional equine term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The course or line of opinion upon which people continue to rely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression for maintaining a settled course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Affected with vehement or intense grief or sorrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate adjectival or nominal use reported in Lane.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sick or very sick, so that the person cannot sit without being propped up.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The condition is defined by dependence on cushions or other supports.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Broken, enervated, or deeply distressed through love; also diseased or sick.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person or heart; the imagery compares the condition with an internally broken camel’s hump.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place or focus of pain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical or descriptive expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Causing pain, especially when applied to the latter part of the night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of a night that causes pain or distress.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tall tent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source notes a possible textual confusion with مُعَمَّدٌ, but preserves the tall-tent interpretation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Set up with poles, especially said of a tent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also applied to a textile figured with the form of lofty buildings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A variegated cloth figured in the form of عِمَاد, understood here as lofty buildings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional textile description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A baptist.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Christian Arabic epithet and likely a borrowed technical term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Held up or supported by columns, especially an object that presses heavily, such as a roof.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Explicitly distinguished from مَدْعُومٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person resorted to in cases of need.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A person treated as an object of reliance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Baptism, or the consecrated baptismal water used by Christians.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The water is described as consecrated by recitation from the Gospel and used for ritual immersion; the word’s Arabic or Syriac origin is disputed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ground, basis, or object of reliance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of what gives a person or matter dependable support.

cautions: The Quranic expression إِرَمَ ذَاتِ الْعِمَادِ has multiple classical interpretations, including lofty buildings, tallness, or both.
The reported أَعْمَدُ idiom is explicitly uncertain and has competing interpretations.
Some non-Quranic Lane entries preserve technical, dialectal, anatomical, figurative, or possibly borrowed uses; these remain separate from Quran-attested meanings.
